statusText: Green - the whole 24-hour window falls inside the CME weekend halt, holding Tail at its structural floor
recommendation: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail sits far below the block threshold and no evidence-based danger window applies, because every published hour falls inside the CME weekend halt and no price path can form. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active as always. The scheduled 22:00Z Sunday futures reopen falls about twelve hours beyond the final slot in this window.
headline: A 3.75-4.00% policy rate, a 10-year near 5% and crude easing back off $106 wait out the weekend halt behind a 14.81 VIX, with Tail at its floor
body: Every hour published here falls inside the CME weekend halt: cash trading ended at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini stopped printing near 21:00Z, and equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, roughly twelve hours after the final slot in this window. Friday's verified marks were re-confirmed at primary sources this hour and stand unchanged. Cash Nasdaq-100 settled at 29,644.17, up 197.17 points or 0.67% from a 29,447.00 previous close, finishing 3.6 points under the top of a 29,371.89-29,647.80 range. VIX fell 4.08% to 14.81 and settled at the low of a 14.80-15.63 daily range. Friday was a quadruple-witching expiry alongside the quarterly index rebalance, and it cleared without disorder; the closing strength carried substantial mechanical flow rather than persistent momentum, which is why it is not read as one-way structure. The week's anchor was Wednesday's FOMC decision: a unanimous 12-0 quarter-point increase to a 3.75-4.00% target range, the first rate increase in three years, framed as support for a timelier return to the 2% goal. The 10-year finished Friday near 5% after a 5bp rise, with the 2-year at 4.67% and the effective funds rate at 3.88%, and pricing had begun to lean toward a further increase in October. Crude eased for a third consecutive session, WTI settling at 100.30 and Brent at 103.87, after Saudi Arabia signalled it would restore roughly half the capacity of its damaged East-West pipeline within days and the full line in about six weeks; that file is easing rather than escalating, though shipping risk near Bab el-Mandeb remains unresolved. Friday's internals were rotational rather than directional, with semiconductor leadership set against evenly split megacaps. Taken together, none of this supplies the persistent directional efficiency, shallow pullbacks or repeated extension after failed retracements that Tail is built to measure, and in a halted market no such path can form at all. Tail therefore holds at 5 through most of the window and lifts only to 6 late on Sunday morning, reflecting the growing stock of headlines that will not be tested by a price until the reopen. Stress stays inside the low band and Confidence decays steadily, describing the staleness of an evidence set that cannot be refreshed while every venue is closed.

lookbackSummary: All 24 preceding hourly assessments were published and every one mapped to green. Tail ran 15-18 through the European morning and the dispersed U.S. cash session, then fell through 16, 11, 7 and 6 as trading ended and the contract settled, holding 5 across the final eleven hours. Stress peaked at 51 during the U.S. afternoon and decayed through 44, 33, 28 and 26 into the halt, reaching 21 across five consecutive slots before ticking to 22. Confidence held between 76 and 88, drifting lower only once the halt removed any refreshing observation. Dominant mode rotated from mixed across the cash session to trend-up into the close, then to normal for the whole post-settlement stretch.
outlookSummary: All 24 published slots fall inside the weekend halt: cash closed at 20:00Z on Friday, the E-mini printed last near 21:00Z, and CME equity futures do not reopen until 22:00Z on Sunday, about twelve hours after the final slot here. Tail is held at 5 through Saturday and the Sunday small hours, lifting to 6 only from 06:00Z as the untested headline stock grows ahead of the reopen; that single point reflects proximity and accumulation, never observed structure. Stress drifts from 22 to 24 and stays inside the low band. Confidence steps down from 75 to 63 across the window, which describes an evidence set ageing without refresh rather than rising danger. Dominant mode is normal throughout, because a closed market cannot express a trend. The identified conditional routes to a gap are the unresolved Middle East shipping and pipeline file, the rates path after a hike that left the 10-year near 5%, and AI or semiconductor headlines landing while no venue can price them; each would become visible only at the reopen, which falls beyond this horizon.
